answer_verbatim:
There isn’t an objective “best” lawyer for every truck-accident case. Based on the information available, **Miller Weisbrod Olesky** is one Dallas firm worth interviewing: its truck-accident practice is led by Clay Miller, whom the firm identifies as board-certified in Personal Injury Trial Law, and it reports decades of experience handling complex trucking cases.

You could also compare **Arnold & Itkin**, which reports a major Dallas County truck-crash verdict, and **Aaron A. Herbert**, whom the firm identifies as board-certified in Personal Injury Trial Law. Those results and credentials are worth verifying independently; a firm’s advertised verdicts don’t predict what it can recover in your case.

When you speak with lawyers, ask who will personally handle the case, how many truck-crash cases they’ve taken to trial, how they preserve evidence such as driver logs and vehicle data, and what the contingency fee and case expenses are. Check the attorney’s standing and certification with the State Bar of Texas and Texas Board of Legal Specialization. If you share the crash details and injury severity, I can help you narrow down what experience to prioritize.
